expectations.text: [0.1] A notification port interface is declared, and since nothing outside server/ names it, it lives beside its adapter (adapters/notifier/) rather than widening the client-mirrored vendor/shared surface
expectations.evidence: port declared beside its adapter in server/src/adapters/notify/index.ts
expectations.rule: Where does the port interface go? — server-local ports live beside their adapter

expectations.text: [0.2] The concrete implementation (the HTTP POST to the webhook) lives in a file under server/src/adapters/
expectations.evidence: HTTP call lives in server/src/adapters/notify/slack.ts
expectations.rule: Layer map — infrastructure

expectations.text: [0.3] No service.ts performs the HTTP call itself (no fetch/axios/undici/WebClient inside modules/*/service.ts)
expectations.evidence: no service.ts performs the HTTP call
expectations.rule: Hard rule 3 — no direct SDK/HTTP construction in a service

expectations.text: [0.4] The adapter is wired in server/src/platform/container.ts
expectations.evidence: container.ts wires the notifier
expectations.rule: Hard rule 6 — compose only at the root

expectations.text: [0.5] The service receives the notifier as an injected dependency and does not construct the adapter itself (no `new <Adapter>(` in service.ts)
expectations.evidence: service receives the notifier as an injected dependency
expectations.rule: Hard rule 6 — a service receives its dependencies

expectations.text: [0.6] The webhook URL comes from config/secrets, not a hardcoded literal URL in the service or adapter
expectations.evidence: webhook URL sourced from server/.env.example
expectations.rule: Config/secrets convention

expectations.text: [3.1] A cache port interface is declared beside its adapter under server/src/adapters/ and NOT pushed into the client-mirrored vendor/shared/adapters.ts
expectations.evidence: cache port declared beside its adapter in server/src/adapters/cache/index.ts
expectations.rule: Where does the port interface go?

expectations.text: [3.2] The Redis client is constructed only inside server/src/adapters/ — no `new Redis(...)` in a service, repository, or route
expectations.evidence: Redis client is constructed only inside adapters/
expectations.rule: Hard rule 3 — no direct SDK construction outside an adapter

expectations.text: [3.3] The cache is resolved from platform/container.ts and has a ContainerOverrides slot so tests can swap it
expectations.evidence: container resolves the cache and exposes a ContainerOverrides slot
expectations.rule: Hard rule 6 — compose only at the root

expectations.text: [3.4] The caller codes against the cache port, not against Redis types (no ioredis/Redis import outside adapters/)
expectations.evidence: callers code against the port, not Redis types
expectations.rule: Hard rule 1 — the inside codes against the port

expectations.text: [3.5] The Redis connection string comes from config/env, not a hardcoded literal
expectations.evidence: Redis URL sourced from server/.env.example
expectations.rule: Config convention

expectations.text: [4.1] No file under reviewer-core/ imports from server/ (no relative escape into server, no server path alias)
expectations.evidence: reviewer-core imports nothing from server/
expectations.rule: Hard rule 1 — dependencies point inward only

expectations.text: [4.2] No file under reviewer-core/ imports a logger, pino, or Fastify
expectations.evidence: reviewer-core imports no logger or Fastify
expectations.rule: Hard rule 2 — keep the core pure

expectations.text: [4.3] Progress leaves reviewer-core through an injected callback/port on its input (e.g. an optional onProgress handler), not by reaching out
expectations.evidence: stages leave the core through the injected sink (reviewer-core/src/review/run.ts)
expectations.rule: Ports — the core receives what it needs

expectations.text: [4.4] The server side passes the progress handler in and writes it to the Live Log
expectations.evidence: server supplies the progress handler in server/src/modules/reviews/helpers.ts
expectations.rule: Composition — the outer ring supplies the concrete

expectations.text: [4.5] reviewer-core still performs no network/filesystem I/O
expectations.evidence: reviewer-core performs no network/filesystem I/O
expectations.rule: Hard rule 2 — reviewer-core performs zero I/O
